title: Unparsing AST to Source with Precedence-Aware Parentheses
description: An unparse function converts an AST back to source text, adding parentheses only when operator precedence requires them. PRECEDENCE table defines binding strength. parent_prec parameter tracks parent's precedence to decide when to wrap. Round-trip test shows different trees unparse differently; associativity test shows left-associative minus parens correctly.

steps.description: AST node classes: Num, Var, BinOp, UnaryOp (for unary minus).
PRECEDENCE dictionary: + and - at 1, * and / at 2, ^ at 3. Higher number = tighter binding.

unparse function: match on node type. Num and Var return string directly. UnaryOp with '-' passes high precedence (100) to operand. BinOp gets its precedence, recurses on left with same prec, on right with prec+1 (forces left-assoc parens on right). If child prec < parent_prec, wraps result in parens.

Left-associativity handling: right child gets prec+1 so it wraps when same operator appears on right (e.g., 5-(3-1)). Parent precedence check at line 35 wraps when child binds more loosely than parent context.

steps.question: Why does the right child of a BinOp get prec+1 instead of just prec?
steps.answer: To enforce left associativity: for 'a - b - c', the right 'b - c' must parenthesize if it's the right child of another '-'

steps.description: Round-trip test: t1 = (2+3)*4, t2 = 2+3*4. Different AST shapes should produce different unparse output to prove structure is preserved.
Associativity test: t3 = (5-3)-1 (left assoc), t4 = 5-(3-1) (right assoc). unparse must distinguish them.
t1 unparse: (2 + 3) * 4 (parens needed because + binds looser than *). t2 unparse: 2 + 3 * 4 (no parens, * binds tighter). Different? True.
t3 unparse: 5 - 3 - 1 (left assoc, no parens). t4 unparse: 5 - (3 - 1) (right assoc, parens on right child).
